title: Harden the fail-closed state-file path: the Stage 1 minor findings on TS-30
description:
Follow-up to the Stage 1 review of opum-ai/test-skills#46 (TS-30). The verdict recorded verbatim on the completed TS-30 record is APPROVE; these are its minor findings that did not block. Filed at the leader's instruction on 2026-10-20. To Do, unclaimed, off the plan.

1. MINOR, gate.py:403-417. The claim that a run reports one violation per bad file is wrong: the try block aborts at the first StateFileError, so with both files corrupt only the first is named and the second surfaces once that is fixed. Still fail-closed. Either say "one per run", or load each file in its own try.

2. MINOR, gate.py:212 vs :215. `ls-tree ... -- path` resolves relative to the cwd (root) while `git show ref:path` resolves from the repo top. With root a subdirectory of the repo and the file present at the base inside that subdirectory, ls-tree says present, show returns empty through the _git swallow, and the gate reports a false unreadable_state_file. It fails closed, not open; the old code had the same mismatch but silently read []. The reverse case cannot happen. Fix with `ref:./path` in show, or `--full-name`. Untested.

5. NIT, test_gate_matrix.py:68,74. Asserting that "quarantine" appears in the message is trivially true because the file name contains it, and the article (XI vs XII) is not asserted, so a mutation that swaps the kind or article labels would survive. Assert the article, and a kind token that is not part of the path.

6. NIT, gate.py:691-696. write_baseline now exits on a corrupt file where it previously swallowed. In the spirit of DEC-213, but it is a behaviour change that nothing tests.

7. NIT, out of scope, noted here so it is not lost: valid JSON of the wrong shape (`{}`, `null`, an entry with no "since") still crashes with a traceback rather than a named violation, at head and at the base.

Findings 3 and 4 from the same review are NOT part of this task.
- Finding 3's advisory-mode half is ruled no-change by DEC-213 (a3): "never passes" binds at blocking levels only, so in advisory mode the violation is a named WARN and the passed field stays true.
- Finding 3's other half, the head lists zeroed when only the base copy was bad, is superseded by DEC-213 (a2): a bad base copy is now treated as empty and zeroes nothing, so there is no separate fix to make.
- Finding 4 is ruled a build by DEC-213 (a2) and is delivered as its own task.

The evidence for every finding is the verbatim verdict on the completed TS-30 record.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A run with both head state files unparseable names both by article and file, not only the first (finding 1).
A repo root below the repo top reads the base copy of its own state file: ls-tree and show resolve the path the same way, so no false unreadable_state_file (finding 2).
The corrupt-head proofs assert the article (XI quarantine, XII probation) and a kind token that is not part of the file name (finding 5).
write_baseline refusing an unparseable state file is covered (finding 6).
Finding 7 (valid JSON of the wrong shape) is out of scope and stays recorded here; findings 3 and 4 are not part of this task.
No collected test case is added beyond the 95 baseline.

implementationNotes:
STAGE 1 VERDICT, recorded verbatim by the opum-marketplace worker at the leader instruction. Reviewer: deepseek-flash (a leader unit, 49/49 turns). Reviewed SHA: d89faa0d4553bc1a127a9e30b5a3d120fbb7ea0b (opum-ai/test-skills#56; landed as 856292f after dev was merged in at 4b11e646875bad3dd35b1f1d899f6a9305b62c29). Source file sha256: 4f376c5a4ad945a3e5109ab991988d73a5023f1c185a78d8adea1449deccf5c4. The verdict text follows unchanged.

VERDICT: APPROVE
REVIEWED SHA: d89faa0d4553bc1a127a9e30b5a3d120fbb7ea0b (confirmed from the worktree's .git → gitdir HEAD; I read the full diff and the post-change tree, read-only, no shell)

(a) Findings, each fixed and proven:
- 1 (both corrupt named): gate.py:421-436 — each head state file loaded in its own try, add() at :428, `continue` at :432, assignment to head_q/head_p at :433-436. Proven at tests/test_gate_matrix.py:77-82, which pins the list to exactly [("XI","unreadable_state_file"),("XII","unreadable_state_file")] and then asserts the file name attaches to the right one in each direction. Correct fix arm: the "one violation per bad file" wording lives only in the completed TS-30 record (grepped **/*.{md,py,json} — only .quest/completed/TS-30.json and TS-35.json), so nothing in code or docs was left stating it falsely; rewording would have had no site to reword.
- 2 (ls-tree vs show): gate.py:217 now `f"{ref}:./{path}"`.
- 5 (trivial assertions): tests/test_gate_matrix.py:66-69 and :73-75 now assert the article from the structured field (XI / XII) and the phrase "is the quarantine state file" / "is the probation state file", which is not part of the path, so a kind or article swap dies.
- 6 (write_baseline): behaviour unchanged by this PR (no hunk near gate.py:714-720); coverage added at tests/test_gate_matrix.py:84-91 — SystemExit raised, message names the probation file, and out.json is asserted not to exist.

(b) Finding 2's chosen fix resolves both arms. ls-tree resolves against the subprocess cwd (= root) and `ref:./path` is git's explicitly cwd-relative revision form, so the two now agree when root is a subdirectory; when root IS the repo top, `./path` is byte-equivalent in effect to `path`, and every other git-backed test in this suite already passes root=repo-top, so a fix that broke that arm would go red there. The subdirectory arm is genuinely exercised at tests/test_gate.py:357-368, and it discriminates: without the fix base_p reads [] and gate.py:649 fires uncertified_demotion, which the first assertion forbids. The quarantine file is not separately exercised under a sub-root, but the fix is inside the one shared helper (_load_list_at), so one arm proves it.

(c) Both corrupt → two violations, each carrying its own article (XI/XII) and its own file. No silent skip: add() runs before `continue` on every path through the loop. A non-ValueError read error still propagates and crashes the run, so it remains fail-closed as before. Advisory mode (R1) still returns passed=True with a named WARN — unchanged, and ruled no-change by DEC-213 (a3).

(d) The side effect is safe and strictly stricter. A retained valid list can only enlarge new_q/new_p (:443-444) and demoted (:453), which can only add XI/XII/II findings at :445-449, :462-465 and :649-651; nothing is suppressed, and the corrupt copy's own violation is still added. No path lets a run pass on a corrupt head file.

(e) No new collected case. The diff adds no `def test_` and no parametrize decorator; every addition is statements inside the existing test_quarantine_windows (4 params) and test_a_new_probation_entry_without_a_matrix_is_flagged. Consistent with the 95 claim, though I could not run pytest to confirm the count.

FINDINGS
1. MINOR — gate.py:556, :627, :658. The identical path-mismatch class survives outside _load_list_at: `rel_t`/`pf`/`rel` are built root-relative (os.path.relpath(..., root), or a policy path that tier matching treats as root-relative) and handed to `git show f"{base}:{rel}"`, which resolves from the repo top. Below a sub-root :556 reads the wrong file or nothing; the "nothing" arm is stricter, but the "wrong file" arm can make self_added too small, so at R4+ a PR could triage its own survivor as equivalent without a listed approver. Narrow and out of the filed scope of finding 2 (which names gate.py:212/:215 only) — recommend a follow-up task rather than changes here.
2. NIT — gate.py:714-718. write_baseline's `hidden` comprehension still aborts at the first StateFileError, so — the same shape as finding 1 — it names only the first corrupt state file. It exits, so it is fail-closed and no "one per file" claim is made there; worth a code comment or the same follow-up.
3. NIT — tests/test_gate_matrix.py:90. Which file the SystemExit message names depends on the tuple order at gate.py:716 (probation first). The assertion is real (a reorder goes red), but it silently pins loop order.
4. NIT — AC index 4 ("finding 7 out of scope, 3 and 4 not part of this task") is checked but no code can satisfy or falsify it. Process nit in the record, not in the change.
5. Note — tests/test_gate.py:357-368 creates a nested git repo under tmp_path; it is placed last in the function, after the parent's final _commit, so nothing stages it. Fine as written, fragile if the block is later moved above a _commit(tmp_path).

Corroboration of the writer's mutation claims from structure alone: restoring the original gate.py should redden the 4 test_quarantine_windows params (both-corrupt block) plus the sub-root block of test_a_new_probation_entry_without_a_matrix_is_flagged = 5, matching its claim; the XI/XII swap reddens only test_quarantine_windows, at 4 params = 4, also matching.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY (no shell): the actual pytest run — 95 collected under -m "not slow", the 5-red and 4-red mutation counts, and CI on this SHA (accepted as leader-verified). I also could not execute git to confirm that `git show ref:./path` resolves in this repo's git version, though the green sub-root test on 3.9 and 3.12 implies it does.
finalSummary: Findings 1, 2, 5 and 6 fixed and proved, 7 left out of scope as filed, 3 and 4 not part of this task. gate.py: each head state file is now loaded in its own try so one run names both when both are unparseable (the "one violation per bad file" claim, which lives only in the completed TS-30 record, is made true rather than reworded; a corrupt quarantine copy also no longer zeroes a valid probation list); the base read uses ref:./path so it resolves like ls-tree when root is below the repo top. Tests are folded into existing cases (test_quarantine_windows, the probation git case): article and a kind token not in the file name are asserted, both-corrupt names both, write_baseline exits on a corrupt file, and a sub-root repo reads its own base copy. No collected case added: -m "not slow" still passes 95. Mutation: restoring the original gate.py turned 5 tests red; swapping the XI/XII labels turned 4 red. Local run Python 3.12 via uv; CI cited at the PR head.
